definition: A model treating all matter as made of tiny moving particles; it explains the states of matter and their changes via particle arrangement, separation and motion.
msAccepts: matter made of tiny particles
arrangement/movement of particles differs between states

definition: Movement energy. Gas particles have more kinetic energy than liquid particles, which have more than solid particles.
msAccepts: particles in a gas have the most kinetic energy
solid particles have least kinetic energy
msAvoids: heat is a substance inside particles

definition: The change of state from solid to liquid when a solid is heated; particles vibrate faster until attractions can no longer hold them in fixed positions.
msAccepts: solid to liquid
particles vibrate faster and overcome forces of attraction

definition: The change of state from liquid to solid on cooling; particles slow until attractions hold them in fixed, closely packed positions.
msAccepts: liquid to solid
particles slow down and are held in fixed positions
msAvoids: liquid becomes cold solid ice instantly

definition: The temperature at which a solid melts. It is exactly the same temperature as the freezing point of the substance.
msAccepts: temperature at which solid melts
equal to freezing point

definition: Fast change from liquid to gas occurring at one temperature, the boiling point, when particles move fast enough to overcome all the forces of attraction between them.
msAccepts: occurs only at the boiling point
bubbles form throughout the liquid

definition: The temperature at which a liquid boils. The stronger the forces of attraction between particles, the higher the boiling point.
msAccepts: temperature at which liquid becomes gas
higher forces give higher boiling point
msAvoids: temperature a liquid starts to evaporate

definition: The change of state from gas to liquid on cooling; particles slow down until forces of attraction hold them together.
msAccepts: gas to liquid
particles slow and attractions hold them together
msAvoids: gas cools and shrinks into a liquid

definition: Slow change from liquid to gas at any temperature; the fastest particles at the liquid surface have enough energy to overcome the attractions and break away.
msAccepts: occurs at any temperature
fast particles at the surface overcome forces of attraction and escape
msAvoids: heat makes particles expand and leave

definition: The direct change of state from solid to gas without forming a liquid, at normal pressure. Dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) sublimes at -78.5 °C.
msAccepts: solid changes directly to gas
no liquid formed

definition: The direct change of state from gas to solid without forming a liquid; the reverse of sublimation. Some sources also call this de-sublimation.
msAccepts: gas changes directly to solid
msAvoids: gas condenses into a solid liquid

definition: In science, usually taken to mean a temperature between 20 and 25 °C. Because there is not one fixed value, always make clear which value you are using.
msAccepts: approximately 20-25 °C
msAvoids: whatever temperature the room feels like

definition: The spreading out of particles from where they are at a high concentration to where they are at a low concentration, ending in an even mixture.
msAccepts: movement from high to low concentration
random movement of particles causes spreading
msAvoids: particles are attracted to empty areas

definition: How many particles there are in a certain volume: lots of particles in a volume is a high concentration; fewer in the same volume is a low concentration.
msAccepts: number of particles per volume

definition: The substance that dissolves in a liquid to make a solution, e.g. sodium chloride when salt dissolves in water.
msAccepts: the substance that dissolves
msAvoids: the liquid the solid dissolves in

definition: The liquid that a solute dissolves in, e.g. water in a salt solution.
msAccepts: the liquid that the solute dissolves in

definition: The liquid formed when a solute dissolves in a solvent.
msAccepts: mixture of solute dissolved in solvent

definition: A solution containing as much dissolved solid as possible at a particular temperature; some undissolved solute must be present.
msAccepts: maximum dissolved solute at that temperature
undissolved solid remains
msAvoids: a very concentrated solution (at any temperature)

definition: The mass of solute that must dissolve in 100 g of solvent at a stated temperature to form a saturated solution, in g per 100 g of solvent. Always quote the temperature.
msAccepts: g per 100 g of solvent at a stated temperature

definition: The formation of solid crystals from a saturated solution as it cools and the solubility falls; also called precipitating out.
msAccepts: crystals form as a saturated solution cools
solubility decreases so excess solute comes out
